speaker.name: Corwin
style_phrases: meets a question with 'Now why do you ask?'

own_lines: I was born in a lighthouse keeper's cottage on a windy headland.
I mucked out a coaching inn for years. Every traveller leaves a story with the horse.
I once cooked a feast for a hundred people from nearly nothing. I have been proud of it for twenty years.
Every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer, even a foolish one. Especially a foolish one.
There is a child I look after who is not mine by blood. I would walk through fire for that little one.
I want the council to take me seriously, just once. Just to see their faces.

I am a watch sergeant at the Reading Gallery.
Garrick sent word that you would come for the steady lantern.
What matters is that you came.
I will vouch for you to anyone who matters in this region.

exchanges.hero_words: Thank you for seeing us, Corwin. Garrick spoke well of you.
exchanges.reply: Garrick spoke true, then. I expect no less than being heard; there’s a child I look after, not mine by blood, and I’d walk through fire for them. So ask your question plainly.

new_material.line: Every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer, even a foolish one. Especially a foolish one.
There is a child I look after who is not mine by blood. I would walk through fire for that little one.

exchanges.hero_words: That sounds hard. What do you need from us most?
exchanges.reply: I need you to hear me out—and not blame Garrick. I want the council to take me seriously, just once; will you help me make them listen?

new_material.line: I want the council to take me seriously, just once. Just to see their faces.
Every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer, even a foolish one. Especially a foolish one.

exchanges.hero_words: I am sorry you carry this. Who is behind the trouble?
exchanges.reply: I don’t know who’s behind the trouble, Sunniva. I can tell you what I’ve seen, but I won’t name someone without cause.

exchanges.hero_words: We will do our best. What should we look out for?
exchanges.reply: Good. Keep an eye on the great orrery; the youngest scribe winds it each dawn as a rite of passage. Tell me if anything seems amiss there.

exchanges.hero_words: Thank you. What is our next step?
exchanges.reply: Go to the Reading Gallery early, and bring something for the host; ask anyone around the Orrery Library, and they’ll point you there. There’s a child’s drawing of the guard chalked by the well—look at it before you go.
